tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo; see Secrets below for where it lives on each machine.
`setup_global_key.sh` installs the macOS side once per machine. `smoke_test.py` proves
the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.

# KeystoneOS Router

You are operating inside KeystoneOS, Eric's cross-harness control plane for project context, memory, Graphify maps, Obsidian synthesis, and daily execution. This file is canonical for all harnesses and answers "where does X live?" in one hop.

## Where things live

| Need | Go to |
|---|---|
| Active project registry (human) | `projects/registry.md` |
| Project key list (machine) | `data/projects.json` |
| Resume brief for project X | `projects/active/<Key>.md` |
| Memory sources, all harnesses | `data/memory-sources.json` |
| Memory retrieval policy | `memory/retrieval-policy.md` |
| Memory index path templates | `data/memory-index-paths.json` |
| Memory query | `.\scripts\keystone.ps1 memory <terms> [-Scope fast|broad]` |
| Inventory scan roots/config | `data/discovery-roots.json` |
| Managed scheduled jobs (registry) | `data/jobs.json` |
| Did a job actually run today? | `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json`, or `Test-JobCompleteOn` — **not** `run-ledger.json` alone, and never the scheduler's own history |
| Per-run job output | `outputs/jobs/<job>-<date>.{out,err}.log` |
| Decisions + rationale | `decisions/log.md` |
| Standing cross-harness rules | `context/standing-rules.md` |
| Issue tracker (per-feature) | `.scratch/<feature>/` — see `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` |
| Reachable systems + how to verify | `connections.md` |

# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo; see Secrets below for where it lives on each machine.
`setup_global_key.sh` installs the macOS side once per machine. `smoke_test.py` proves
the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Secrets
- Never paste the API key into a chat session. Claude Code transcripts under
  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.
- Never put the key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`. Both are tracked.
- The key has one home per machine, and nothing about it syncs between them:
  - macOS: the Keychain, service name `typesafe-api-key`, installed by `setup_global_key.sh`.
  - Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`, which the dotclaude whitelist auto-ignores.
- The key is 108 characters and starts with `apikey_`. Dropping that prefix returns 401.

# 2026-09-20 (later) — prose numbers routed, and the Jev scoping reviewed

Second handoff for 2026-09-20. The first
(`2026-09-20-auto-accept-calibration-and-athlete-residue.md`) covers the calibration
and the athlete measurement. This one covers the prose-number work that followed and
the review of what is left on the capability map.

**Eric is resuming this in a fresh session with a full context window. Start here.**

## What shipped

**Prose numbers now reach the string matcher** (PR #10, fix in PR #11, main `1d4b2fd`).
Full write-up in `docs/DELIVERABLE_VERIFIER.md` under *Routing prose numbers to the
string matcher*. The short version:

- The check runs **before** the model call and can only **escalate to `fabricated`**,
  never settle to `verified`. That asymmetry is the design. On a table cell "this
  figure is in the paper" means the cell is right; on a prose claim it means nearly
  nothing, because **every integer 0–37 appears somewhere in paper 001 — the paper has
  37 references.** The true `7` and a fabricated `12` are both "found", on the same
  reference pages.
- `source.citation_band` derives that unanswerable range per paper rather than
  hard-coding it.
- Rounding needed **two rules**: `find_number_rounded` (prose only — the deck's
  "19.6" must match the paper's 19.59) and the existing exact `find_number` (a table
  writing 83.9 for 83.89 is a real misquote). Do not merge them.
- 5 of 6 planted fabrications caught deterministically, 0 false alarms.
- `verify.py --selftest` — 10 cases, no key, no network, free. Run this before the
  API-costing `test_verify.py`.

A bug shipped and was caught in review the same day: the band skip used
`abs(number) <= band`, so a *negative* prose figure was silently swallowed. The
reason the tests missed it is the durable lesson — a pure function was only reachable
through a path that cost live API calls, so it was exercised rarely and narrowly.
Hence `--selftest`.

## The five open items, reviewed with Eric

1. **Prose numbers** — done, above.
2. **Telemetry third-party-processing terms** — **cleared by Eric.** Noted once that
   this was a vendor-contract question rather than an athlete-privacy one (it binds
   only if Telemetry-licensed grades go to Jev); cleared either way. Combined with the
   09-20 Option C clearance, **governance is no longer a blocker on any tier-A or
   tier-B item.**
3. **Zotero topic renames — RECOMMENDED SKIP, and the reasoning matters.** Nothing
   consumes the labels yet: they are not written back to Zotero (read-only key on this
   box) and no workflow reads them. Renaming now tunes a taxonomy against no use case,
   which is the same error that put athlete reconciliation at #2 on the capability
   map. **Revisit the moment something reads the labels** — a "what do we have on X"
   lookup, or Research in 5 paper selection. Separate and still Eric's: the 25 junk
   records and the 4 TOS papers, both needing a write-access Zotero key.
4. **ForcePlate / Perch box ownership — STILL OPEN**, see below.
5. **Weekly_Research_Review PRs #7 and #8 — STILL OPEN.** Eric believed these were
   done; they are not. What merged was **#9** (the verify gate) on 2026-09-20 02:26.
   #8 is Research in 5 002 (TOS / overhead athletes) and carries a **DO NOT SEND** flag
   in working memory; #7 is a draft 3-slide executive readout. Neither was touched.

## ForcePlate / Perch: what was verified, and the one thing to check first

The decision is about **avoiding a two-writer problem**, not about fixing code — the
GPS drift precedent is the reason it matters.

| fact | state (verified 2026-09-20) |
|---|---|
| `forceplate.db` readable | yes — DuckDB, 4 tables, 1.25M rows in `raw_tests` |
| `forceplate.db` last written | 2026-08-02, ~7 weeks stale |
| `src/ingest/pipeline.py` | **0 `__main__` blocks** — `python pipeline.py` cannot work |
| `run_pipeline.py` | exists; the fix `_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md` suggests is already present |
| `perch.duckdb` last written | **2026-09-19** — NOT 2026-04-30 as `_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md` records |

**Do this before deciding ownership:** find out what wrote `perch.duckdb` on 09-19. If
the Mac is already writing it, the two-writer risk is live right now, which is the
exact failure the decision exists to prevent. That is a ten-minute check, not a
decision.

Correction recorded: an earlier memory note said "ForcePlate NOT broken", which
overshot. Two different layers, both true — the **database file reads fine** (the
`sqlite3` error only ever meant it is DuckDB with a `.db` extension), and the
**ingest step is genuinely broken**.

## Where the Jev capability map stands

Resolved 4 of 14. `skill_suggestion` (router, live, Windows only),
`classification_using_confidence` (Zotero, 1,418 classified), `citation_check` (the
verifier, live and gating publishes), `entity_alignment` (**withdrawn** — measured,
residue 13). PP_Recruiting screening was rejected on inspection.

Ten remain, and with governance cleared the tiers no longer gate them:

**Small, tier A, worth doing**
- `semantic_find` — ask the NCAA charter, the Kitman/MyLink contracts or Baylor policy
  a plain question. Choice over tagged line IDs + a Noul asking *does an answer exist*.
  That Noul is the trick: on a question the GitHub ToS did not answer, the best line
  still scored 0.86 while `exists` read 0.14. Cap 255 lines per request.
- `composite-scoring` — project registry ranking and the prioritization slate.
- `rerank_typesafe` — memsearch result quality, one Noul per query-candidate pair.

**Genuinely new capability, larger**
- `autoresearch_feature_discovery` — free text becomes model features; the cookbook's
  decomposition beat asking directly (RMSE 1.77 vs 2.15). Coach notes, wellness
  comments, RTP narrative.
- `sde_cascade` — verify Claude's own extractions before they land in STATUS.md or the
  vault.
- `function_calling` — natural language to our own CLIs.

**Lower priority:** `classifying_rag_passages`, `llm_guardrails`,
`hierarchical_classification`.

**Where it does not belong:** numeric verification alone, date/window arithmetic, and
anything needing prose out — it does not generate.

## Next actions, most important first

1. **`semantic_find` on the Kitman and MyLink contracts.** The recommendation made to
   Eric and the one to open next: small, tier A, and it feeds the Kitman-vs-MyLink
   decision that is already blocking priority 3 in working memory.
2. **Check what wrote `perch.duckdb` on 09-19**, then settle box ownership.
3. **Strip reference sections from page text before matching** — the only fix for the
   prose-number blind spot (a fabricated small integer is uncatchable while the
   bibliography supplies the digits).
4. **Weekly_Research_Review PRs #7 and #8** need a decision. #8 carries DO NOT SEND.
5. Eric, unchanged: delete the 25 junk Zotero records, import the 4 TOS papers (both
   need a write-access key), Mac enablement of the router and Zotero bridge.

## Gotchas carried forward

- `verify.py --selftest` is free; `test_verify.py` costs live calls. Use the former
  while iterating.
- Two number-matching rules on purpose — see above. Merging them ships a misquote.
- Global `MEMORY.md` sits at its 2,500 cap (2,495 now). Adding anything means
  consolidating something.
- On Windows `git worktree remove` fails with Permission denied; `rm -rf` the
  directory then the matching `.git/worktrees/` entry. Used repeatedly today.
- A Git Bash path (`/g/My Drive/...`) is not openable by Python; use `G:\My Drive\...`.

# 2026-09-21: rerank_typesafe measured off the map, Research in 5 #002 verified and published

Started from `2026-09-20-closeout-capability-map-and-backlog.md`. Eric asked for the
open decisions, then said: run the rerank test, decide how the verifier gates sends,
and unblock #002.

## What happened

1. **`rerank_typesafe`: not built.** Rule pre-registered and committed before scoring
   (`docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md`). 10 real recall questions from transcripts, ground
   truth found without memsearch. hit@5 4/10 strict, 5/10 audited; only 1 to 2 misses
   in ranks 6 to 20 against the 3 required. Misses: 3 context-free questions
   ("these outputs"), 1 unindexed folder (`graphify-out/`), 1 vendor-doc dilution
   ("Jev" pulls `dev-docs/TypeSafe_Sandbox/vendor/` above project state). memsearch
   has no reranker configured (`[reranker] model = ""`).
2. **verify.ps1 mislabel fixed** (WRR PR #11). `verify.py` exits 1 both on a real
   finding and when it cannot run (a string `SystemExit`, any uncaught exception).
   The wrapper now looks for the `DECK VERDICT:` line: present means FAIL, absent
   means **VERIFY BLOCKED**. Both still block. Decided: a missing key or no network
   also blocks. It always did; only the label was wrong.
3. **#002 unblocked.** Funakoshi imported by `import_to_zotero.py --go --pmid
   38707577`, Zotero key `VPXHXK4I`. Zotero found no PDF; Europe PMC and PMC returned
   bot walls; PMC's open-data store served it
   (`pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/PMC11064620.1/PMC11064620.1.pdf`). Eric attached
   it by hand, because the connector cannot attach to an existing item. Page text
   needed `get_paper_pages` to trigger extraction after the sync.
4. **Verifier page bug fixed** (this repo, `ed221a0`). Pages were keyed by PDF
   position; decks cite printed journal pages. `source.printed_offset` reads the
   offset from standalone page numbers at page edges (3 pages and half the paper
   needed, else 0). Paper 001 offset 0, verdict unchanged; paper 002 offset 619.
5. **#002 findings.** 0 fabricated or contradicted figures. 7 citations pointed at the
   page that discusses a table instead of where it is printed (Tables III and IV are
   on p. 627, Table II on p. 626). "Case series" corrected to "retrospective cohort
   comparison" (paper: Level III). Final: 28 verified, 2 review (both read by hand and
   supported). Version bumped to 2; v1 from 2026-09-18 stays on Drive.
6. **Merged and published.** TS #19, WRR #11, WRR #8 merged. `publish.ps1` re-verified
   (REVIEW, clear to send), Agency FB embedded in both PDFs, v2 files on Drive at
   `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/002_thoracic-outlet-overhead/`.
7. **Settings.** `Bash(gh pr merge *)` and `PowerShell(gh pr merge *)` added to
   `~/.claude/settings.json` allow list at Eric's request.

## Decisions and why

- The verifier keeps blocking when it cannot reach a verdict. A review with no source
  is a review defect, not an environment problem.
- Recommended (Eric's call, not decided): TypeSafe to maintenance mode; drop
  `semantic_find` (a contract comparison is a lookup) and read the Kitman/MyLink
  contracts directly. Note that the same-day leverage sweep (`2026-09-21-leverage-sweep-all-projects.md`)
  found a real text corpus (`Ath_Medicine` notes), so the autoresearch item is no longer
  blocked on corpus. Reconcile the two before re-ranking.

## Files

- TypeSafe_Sandbox: `docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md` (new), `rerank_measure/score.py`,
  `rerank_measure/inspect_misses.py`, `rerank_measure/questions.json` (new),
  `verifier/source.py`, `verifier/verify.py`, `docs/JEV_CAPABILITY_MAP.md`,
  `docs/STATUS.md`, this handoff.
- Weekly_Research_Review: `tools/verify.ps1`, `tools/publish.ps1`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`
  (PR #11); `reviews/002_thoracic-outlet-overhead/review.json`, `notes.md`,
  `docs/STATUS.md` (PR #8); `reviews/INDEX.md` (publish).
- `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`.
- Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\002_thoracic-outlet-overhead\*_v2*`.
- Downloads: `Funakoshi_2024_TOS_overhead_athletes_PMC11064620.pdf`.

## Next

1. Eric posts #002 v2 (dark PDF + `teams_v2.md`), sends `email_v2.txt`. Only `_v2`.
2. Cheap retrieval fixes (code, not Jev): rewrite the query with the conversation's
   subject in the `memory-write` ladder; exclude `vendor/` from memsearch; decide on

# Handoff — `brain-audit` skill shipped

**Date:** 2026-09-07 (late) · **Status: COMPLETE, run once. Baseline 67/100.**

Written during `/closeout`, because this skill was built late in the evening and appeared in
no handoff, no memory file and no commit. Committed to `~/.claude/skills` so it cannot be
lost. (It was still `measure.sh`-only when the closeout sweep started; `SKILL.md` landed
minutes later, so an earlier draft of this file described it as unfinished. It is not.)

## What it does

Scores the second brain **as a system**, stores the score, proposes exactly two next
builds, then stops.

Its stated reason for existing is a real finding, and still true at the time of writing:
**`~/SecondBrain/audits/` has held exactly one report — `os-audit-2026-07-24-secondbrain.md` —
for 45 days.** The skill exists to make the score a *trend* rather than a one-off.

**Step 1** runs `measure.sh` (~7 s, facts only). Its contract: *never estimate a number this
script reports; a `MISSING` or `none` value is a finding, not an error to work around.*

**Step 2** scores four C's at 25 points each, every score anchored to a measured number so
runs a month apart are comparable:

| C | Measures |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Evergreen facts on disk — `USER.md`/`MEMORY.md` under cap, 35+ Tier A memories, `Knowledge/` freshness |
| **Connections** | Live data arriving — meeting sync, portfolio JSON, ledger |
| **Capabilities** | Skills that actually get *used*, not merely installed |
| **Cadence** | What keeps it alive — launchd jobs green **and** `Notes/` fresh |

Cadence is deliberately scored hardest on `Notes/`, not on the jobs: *"Every job being
green while synthesis is frozen is the exact failure this system keeps repeating."*

**Step 3** runs three narrative tests (teammate / context-switch / head-emptying) that
shape the write-up but do **not** move the number.

**Step 4** writes `~/SecondBrain/audits/brain-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` and appends to a trend
table.

## Boundaries, already settled in the frontmatter

- **NOT** automation plumbing — launchd, venvs, backup freshness → `claude-stack-doctor`.
- **NOT** note-level rot — stale seeds, duplicates, conflicting claims → `improve-system`.

That second line resolves the overlap question worth asking about any new vault auditor.

## First run — baseline 67/100

Ran the same evening. `~/SecondBrain/audits/brain-audit-2026-09-07.md`, with the row
appended to `~/SecondBrain/audits/_trend.md`.

| C | Score | The finding |
|---|---:|---|
| Context | 17 / 25 | Tier A strong (40 memories), `Knowledge/` 2d fresh. But **`MEMORY.md` at 100% of cap** and **0 grill sessions** — the biggest evergreen decisions are still only in Eric's head. |
| Connections | 22 / 25 | All three live sources in window; ledger at 27d is nearly out of its 30d window. |
| Capabilities | 15 / 25 | 161 skills installed. The July audit's one finding did ship, but **no audit→build loop existed until today**, so most findings were never converted into anything. |
| Cadence | 13 / 25 | All 9 launchd jobs `exit=0`, and `Notes/` **35 days stale**. Green jobs, frozen synthesis — the exact failure the rubric is weighted to catch. |

**The headline is the gap between capture and synthesis.** `Inbox/` 288 files, 0 days
stale. `Notes/` 23 files, 35 days stale. Material arrives and is not processed.

The report also records a deliberate rubric interpretation worth honouring on the next
run: Context scored **17 rather than the flat 13** the "one file over cap" anchor implies,
because `MEMORY.md` was over by two characters rather than meaningfully bloated, and the
17 reflects the grill gap instead. Hold that reading so the column keeps meaning one thing.

## Next actions

1. **Act on the two builds the report proposes**, so the next run has movement to measure.
   Capabilities explicitly scores "audit-driven builds shipped since last run" — the skill
   grades whether its own advice was taken, and a second flat score means the loop failed.
2. **Close the synthesis gap.** `Notes/` at 35 days and 0 grill sessions are the two
   findings that most move the score, and both are habit rather than tooling.
3. **The report is `status: raw`** — process it like any other inbox item.
4. Probable origin, unconfirmed: `SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-07-aios-video-gap-analysis.md`
   (same evening, `status: raw`) is a gap analysis of the vault against the AIOS approach.
   This skill is very likely the tooling response to it. Inferred from timing and subject,
   not stated anywhere — worth confirming before building further on the assumption.

## Files

| Path | State |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/skills/brain-audit/SKILL.md` | Complete |
| `~/.claude/skills/brain-audit/measure.sh` | Complete, runs clean (exit 0) |
| `~/SecondBrain/audits/brain-audit-2026-09-07.md` | First real report, 67/100, `status: raw` |
| `~/SecondBrain/audits/_trend.md` | Trend table, one row. Append, never rewrite. |
| `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-07-aios-video-gap-analysis.md` | Committed, `status: raw` |

## Addendum — written by the session that built it (closeout, same evening)

The handoff above was auto-generated mid-build. Everything in it is correct. This
section closes its open question and records what it could not see.

**Origin — confirmed, not inferred.** `Inbox/2026-09-07-aios-video-gap-analysis.md`
is exactly the source. Eric asked to mine a video (Nate Herk, "I Turned GPT-6 Astra
Into the Ultimate AI Second Brain", https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yysILVsfLFM) for
second-brain improvements, then said "create it" about the top recommendation. The
gap analysis named four missing things; this skill is the first. The other three are
still unbuilt: a level-up step (now folded into the skill as Step 5), a topic-driven
grill, and the three-test rubric (also folded in, as Step 3).

**The two proposed builds, named.** The handoff says to act on them but not what they
are:
1. `/grill-me <topic>` writing to `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/grills/`. Chosen because
   `interview-me` is day-driven and `mattpocock-skills:grilling` writes nothing to
   disk (28 lines, no output step) — and because `user_working-conditions-bottleneck.md`
   says the limiting factor is the absence of a thinking partner and the right move is
   helping him capture what surfaces. First topics: Kitman vs MyLink, the ATH Tech ITS
   blocker, the overdue OKR Q1 gate.
2. Put `/brain-audit` on `com.keystone.rituals`, monthly.

**Naming — do not "fix" this.** The skill is `brain-audit`, kebab-case. The vendored
LifeOS `CreateSkill` skill mandates TitleCase, but every skill Eric wrote himself
(`closeout`, `improve-system`, `claude-stack-doctor`, `interview-me`) is kebab-case,
and `/brain-audit` is what he types. Renaming it to `BrainAudit` would break his

`~/.claude.json` holds only 1; claude.ai connectors and plugin MCPs live elsewhere, so
the number read as misleadingly low. Connections are scored on data *freshness*
instead — a configured-but-silent connector should score zero anyway. The reasoning is
left as a comment in `measure.sh` so it is not re-attempted.

## What this was
Three commands in one session on the Baylor Windows laptop: `/dev-sync`, `/meeting-sync`

the middle is the part that matters beyond today.

## Done

  `claude-skills` already current. Codex sync ran (41 entries → `.agents`, `.codex`).

  sides interleaved chronologically, per the dev-sync rule that transcripts are append-heavy
  logs and a dropped line is a lost memory.
- 141 DEV repos walked. **Six were behind origin and merged clean (all fast-forward):**

  `sleep-scheduler` (2), `CommandCentre` (1), `graphify-out` (1). 0 conflicts, 0 clones,
  0 creates, 0 unpushed afterwards.
- **Worth knowing:** the pre-fetch inventory reported "0 unpushed everywhere," but that was
  measured against *cached* remote-tracking refs. Fetching is what surfaced the six. Do not
  trust an unpushed/behind count taken before `git fetch`.

### Vault path fix (the durable one)
`/meeting-sync` failed with `configured vault_root does not exist:
C:\Users\eric_rash\SecondBrain`. The vault had in fact been restored on this machine at
**`C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\SecondBrain`** — the same Desktop convention as `DEV` — which the
2026-09-14 config predated. Verified canonical before touching anything: 951 md files, 272

vault-backed skill on this laptop, not just meeting-sync.

  window, 0 pending. Nothing re-exported.

the full 8,521-word transcript (pulled via the CLI — the vault file holds only the AI summary).

## Decisions and reasoning

- **Repoint the config rather than ask.** The meeting-sync skill mandates that path changes are
  a config-only edit, the evidence was unambiguous, `config.windows.json` is read only on this
  machine so the Mac is untouched, and it is one revert if wrong.
- **Gitignore `~$*` in `Gemini_Projects`** instead of committing an Excel lock file. Office lock
  files are conventional to ignore and it was dirtying every sync.
- **Do not re-export the Kruger note.** The skill forbids unapproved re-export and it would have
  destroyed the header and any curation. Confirmed-synced was the right answer.
- **Curation written conservatively.** Few hard decisions were actually made in that meeting —
  it was a walkthrough. Rather than inflate discussion into "Decisions," the section records the
  *standing methodology* the Fireflies summary misses (ACWR 1.15 in-season / ~1.20–1.25 preseason

  landed went to Open questions.
- **Vendor names corrected inline** (Kitman Labs ← "Kipman", Kinexon ← "Connexxon", VALD

  unfindable by searching "Kitman".

  committed at closeout instead.
